title: Nest N1 — internal battery low
shortDescription: Internal lithium battery has dropped below 3.6V and cannot sustain operation.
fullDescription:
Nest Learning and Nest Thermostat E use a rechargeable internal battery kept topped up by power stealing or by a C-wire. An N1 code indicates battery voltage has fallen too low to operate reliably — usually because no C-wire is installed and power stealing isn't delivering enough current.

Disconnect the unit and charge via micro-USB (or USB-C on newer models) for 1-2 hours. Once it boots, install a C-wire for permanent operation.

Chronic N1 on a system with a C-wire suggests an aging internal battery and may need warranty service.

fixSteps.title: USB charge
fixSteps.instruction: Remove from base and charge via USB for 1-2 hours.

fixSteps.title: Install C-wire
fixSteps.instruction: Add a dedicated C-wire or Nest Power Connector.

whenToCallPro: If C-wire is already present and battery still fails, contact Google Nest warranty.
videoSearchQuery: Nest thermostat N1 error battery fix

faq.a: Not user-serviceable; Nest replaces the unit.

title: Nest N2 — no charging voltage
shortDescription: Battery is not receiving charging current from HVAC power.
fullDescription:
The N2 error indicates the thermostat detected no charging source. Unlike N1 (battery critically low), N2 appears when voltage at the base is insufficient to charge at all. Usually the Rh-to-base line is absent or the low-voltage fuse has blown.

Verify 24VAC between Rh and C. If absent, check the 3A fuse on the furnace control board.
symptoms: Shuts off when removed from USB

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Replace blown 3A fuse on control board.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Rh
fixSteps.instruction: Push Rh wire firmly into terminal, confirm button clicks.

whenToCallPro: If transformer failed, call HVAC pro.
videoSearchQuery: Nest N2 error not charging fix

faq.q: Is N2 the same as N1?
faq.a: Related — N1 is low battery, N2 is no charging source.

title: Nest N26 — cannot read thermostat serial
shortDescription: Internal read failure of device serial number; usually firmware corruption.
fullDescription:
The N26 code appears when the thermostat cannot verify its own serial number, typically after a bad firmware update or internal memory error. A factory reset often resolves it.

Remove from base, charge via USB, then perform Settings > Reset > All Settings. If reset fails, Google Nest warranty replacement is typically required.
symptoms: Won't pair with Google Home app

fixSteps.title: Charge via USB
fixSteps.instruction: USB charge for 30 min to ensure full boot.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: If reset fails, request replacement via Google Nest support.

whenToCallPro: If reset does not clear, contact Google Nest warranty.

faq.a: Yes — but schedules resync from the Google Home app.

title: Nest N260 — thermostat offline, will not respond
shortDescription: Nest cloud reports thermostat offline for extended period; usually Wi-Fi/router issue.
fullDescription:
N260 means the Google Nest service has not heard from your thermostat for an extended period. The thermostat is usually running fine locally but cannot reach the cloud. Router problems, ISP outages, and DNS misconfiguration are the main causes.

Restart the router and reconnect Wi-Fi on the thermostat.
whenToCallPro: If persistent after Wi-Fi fixes, contact Google Nest support.

title: Nest W1 — Wi-Fi disconnected
shortDescription: Thermostat cannot connect to local Wi-Fi.
fullDescription: W1 appears when the thermostat lost the Wi-Fi link. Most common causes are password changes, 5GHz-only SSIDs, or weak signal. Nest supports 802.11 b/g/n on 2.4GHz (and 5GHz on the 2020 model and Learning Gen 3).

fixSteps.title: Rejoin network
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Network > select SSID > enter password.

fixSteps.title: Move router
fixSteps.instruction: Reposition or add a mesh node if signal is weak.

title: Nest W5 — Wi-Fi chip error
fullDescription: W5 indicates a hardware-level issue with the Wi-Fi module. Reboot clears software glitches; if it persists, the radio itself has failed.
whenToCallPro: Hardware Wi-Fi failure requires warranty replacement.

faq.a: No — W5 is hardware, W1 is connection.

title: Nest E74 — Rh power issue
shortDescription: Rh terminal not detecting adequate voltage.
fullDescription: E74 indicates Nest sees no or intermittent voltage on Rh. On systems with separate Rh/Rc, verify both wires land in their correct terminals. A blown furnace fuse or tripped float switch is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fuse and float
fixSteps.instruction: Replace fuse; clear condensate if float tripped.

whenToCallPro: Call HVAC pro if wiring is unclear.

faq.a: No — it just halts HVAC calls.

title: Nest E195 — no Rc detected
shortDescription: Thermostat does not detect voltage on Rc (cooling transformer).
fullDescription: E195 usually appears on dual-transformer systems where Rc is not connected or the cooling transformer has failed. Single-transformer systems should use a Rh-Rc jumper or the thermostat's auto-jumper.

causes.cause: Rc not wired on dual-transformer system
Rh-Rc jumper missing on single-transformer system

fixSteps.title: Add Rh-Rc jumper
fixSteps.instruction: On single-transformer systems, insert a short wire from Rh to Rc.

title: Nest E298 — internal hardware fault
fullDescription: E298 is a generic internal hardware fault code. Try factory reset once; if it returns, contact Google Nest support for warranty replacement.

title: Nest no power detected on Rh or Rc
shortDescription: Display is blank or Nest reports no 24V on either power terminal.
fullDescription: Without Rh (heating transformer) or Rc (cooling transformer) power, Nest will not run. Check the 3A HVAC fuse, furnace access switch, and confirm transformer output.

fixSteps.title: Check furnace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure panel closed and switch on.

fixSteps.title: Replace 3A fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Swap blade fuse on control board.

title: Nest battery keeps dying
shortDescription: Thermostat repeatedly drops to low battery even with HVAC wiring.
fullDescription: Chronic battery drain means power stealing is inadequate. Install a C-wire or Nest Power Connector to deliver continuous 24V. Heavy Wi-Fi use and Farsight drain the battery faster than power stealing can replenish.

fixSteps.title: Install C-wire
fixSteps.instruction: Add C-wire or Nest Power Connector.

whenToCallPro: If C-wire is already present, request warranty replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Nest battery dying fix C wire

title: Nest E300 — sensor read error
shortDescription: Temperature or humidity sensor failed self-check.
fullDescription: E300 indicates the internal sensor returned an implausible reading. Reboot and firmware update usually clears; persistent failures need warranty.
whenToCallPro: After reset and firmware attempts fail.
